div.head: Abt 20
div.ab: Gif man þone man ofslæhð, XX scillingum gebete.
Gif man þone man ofslæhð, XX scillingum gebete.
Gif man þone man of slæhð, XX scillingum gebete.
wenn man aber [damit] einen Menschen erschlägt, büsse [der Waffendarleiher an dessen Sippe] mit 20 Schillingen.
but if a person is slain [with them], let [the lender of the weapons] pay [to his kin] 20 shillings.
If the man is slain, [the lender of the weapons] shall pay 20 shillings compensation.
If, however, a man is killed, he is to pay 20 shillings compensation.
If a person kills that man [who is being robbed] let him [i.e., the one who provided the weapons] pay with 20 shillings.

note.label: cf.
note.quote: Æthelberht §23.2 [L20] requires that the man who loaned the weapon pay 20 shillings.

div.note: The man who provided the weapon.

note.seg: þone kann demonstrativ ‘jenen’ bedeuten, nämlich den laut 19 Beraubten. Allein der Gesetzgeber wollte doch wohl den Darleiher haften lassen für Totschlag überhaupt, nicht bloss Raubmord, mit der ihm entliehenen Waffe. Daher nehm ich þone für þonne (s. d. Wb 223 Sp. 2), eine sowohl für frühestes Agsä. (Sweet Oldest texts 581) wie für Mittelenglisch (Morris Specimens 520), also für Abt wie für den Schreiber H mögliche Form

þone can mean demonstratively ‘that one’, namely the man robbed according to 19. But the legislator surely meant to make the lender liable for any homicide committed with the weapon borrowed from him, not merely for murder in the course of robbery. I therefore take þone for þonne (see that word in Wb 223 col. 2), a form possible both in earliest A.-S. (Sweet Oldest texts 581) and in Middle English (Morris Specimens 520), and thus both for Abt and for the scribe H
Den Rest des Wergeldes zahlt der Totschläger; anderwärts beträgt die Haftung (s. d. Gl 4a) eine Quote des Wergeldes
The slayer pays the rest of the wergild; elsewhere the liability (see that word in Gl 4a) amounts to a fraction of the wergild
Es ist wohl nicht bloss zufällig dieselbe Summe für Bewehrung des Angreifers wie u. 24 für Bindung (also Wehrlosmachung) des Angegriffenen
It is probably no mere coincidence that the sum for arming the attacker is the same as that for binding (i.e. rendering defenceless) the person attacked, below 24

The man robbed, in cap. 19; presumably also the man with whom the borrower of the weapons is quarrelling. Liebermann suggests that þone may be used for þonne, which would make the statement general: ‘If however a man is slain (by the borrowed weapons), etc.’ The rarity of þonne elsewhere in these laws is somewhat against Liebermann’s view; for a similar use of the demonstrative, cf. cap. 28 below; for the whole passage cf. Alf. cap. 19 § 1.
